sections.h2: Who bills and collects Carter County property tax?
sections.html:
Three courthouse offices split the job in Carter County. The Property Valuation Administration puts a value on each parcel, the county clerk prints the bills and inherits the unpaid ones, and the sheriff takes payments through the autumn and winter. You will find all three at 300 West Main Street in Grayson, so one visit can settle most questions.

The county is a long stretch of northeastern Kentucky with about 412 square miles of land and water. Greenup and Lawrence counties gave up the ground for it in 1838. Grayson is the seat and Olive Hill is the only other city, which means most of the 12,206 housing units counted in 2020 are rural parcels, farm tracts and older frame houses billed as county property.

sections.h2: Where do I go for Carter County tax questions?
sections.html:
Start with the office that matches the question: value goes to the PVA, a bill amount or payment goes to the sheriff, and anything already delinquent goes to the clerk. The county's official directory lists the details below.

sections.h2: What kind of houses and neighborhoods does Carter County have?
sections.html:
Mostly owner-occupied homes outside town limits, many of them decades old. The 2020 census found 10,664 households, with 75.7 percent of occupied units owned and 12.6 percent of all units empty. Only about one resident in five lived in an area the census treats as urban. The county population was 26,627 in 2020 and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 26,149.

The landscape explains the housing. A through rail route between Lexington and Ashland, later the Chesapeake & Ohio line, reached the county in 1881, and fire clay and refractory brick plants at Olive Hill and Hitchins were major industries in the early and mid 1900s. The Olive Hill depot, built in 1910, is on the National Register of Historic Places. Today Interstate 64 and US 60 carry traffic through the county, and the Carter County School District runs the public schools.

  • Carter Caves State Resort Park lies inside the county line.
  • Kentucky Christian University is in Grayson.
  • Adjoining counties are Greenup, Boyd, Lawrence, Elliott, Rowan and Lewis.

sections.h2: What do Carter County owners pay, and when?
sections.html:
The statewide calendar in KRS 134.015 governs. Your bill arrives near the start of October, and the total you owe depends on the day you pay.

  • Through November 1, a full payment earns 2 percent off.
  • From November 2 to year end, the printed amount is due.
  • All of January adds a 5 percent penalty.
  • Once February begins, the penalty becomes 10 percent and the sheriff's add-on fee applies.

The law treats the tax as your personal debt from the assessment date, and a lien on the land lasts eleven years no matter who buys it. Call the sheriff at (606) 474-5616 if a bill does not show up, and ask that office how it accepts mailed or in-person payments.

sections.h2: How can a Carter County owner contest a valuation?
sections.html:
Begin with the PVA, because Kentucky makes a conference there the entry ticket to every later step. The state opens each county's roll to the public for thirteen days from the first Monday of May, and the conference has to take place before or during that window.

If talking to the PVA does not move the number, deliver a written petition to the county clerk by the next workday after the window closes. Say which parcel is involved and what you think it would fetch on the open market. A local board then hears the case roughly a month later. It looks for proof, such as sale listings, construction costs and insurance policies, and it denies petitions that come without any. Owners who skip the board lose the right to go on to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals.

Filing never stops the clock on payment. You owe tax on the figure you claimed until the case ends, and a higher final value brings a supplemental bill.

sections.h2: What happens to Carter County bills still unpaid in mid-April?
sections.html:
They leave the sheriff and land on the county clerk's desk on April 15. Each one becomes a certificate of delinquency, and the clerk reports that totals jump by about 40 percent once the added charges are counted. Personal checks do not work for these bills, while cash, money orders, company checks and cards (with a user fee) do.

The clerk will sometimes arrange a payment plan: a third of the balance up front and the remainder within 90 days. Miss the deadline and the bill returns to the delinquent list, and the money already paid is kept and credited rather than refunded.

  • The clerk places an ad about 30 days ahead of the sale and posts the list online.
  • The sale for 2024 bills took place August 29, 2025, at 10 am in the fiscal courtroom.
  • Bidders sign up at least ten days beforehand, and the lien assignment fee is $46.

A successful bidder gets the right to collect from you, so settling before April 15 is far cheaper.

sections.h2: Which Carter County owners get a homestead break?
sections.html:
Retirees and owners with a total disability who live in the house they own. The state takes a fixed sum off the assessed value before it applies the rate, and the sum stood at $49,100 for the assessment years 2025 and 2026. On a house assessed at $120,000, the taxable portion would shrink to $70,900. Apply at the Carter County PVA, which also knows the current figure, since it is reset every second year.

A birth certificate, driver's license or passport proves age. Disability applicants renew yearly, with exceptions for veterans with a service-connected rating and owners found permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: How do I sell a Carter County house that still owes tax?
sections.html:
Yes, you can, because the title company pays the balance out of your price. First ask the sheriff for a payoff on this year's bill and ask the clerk whether any older year was filed as delinquent. A recorded certificate appears in a title search and must be paid or released for the buyer to receive clear title.

Timing matters. A bill still with the sheriff carries only the 5 or 10 percent penalty, while one at the clerk adds fees and interest. When the house is inherited, vacant or short on repairs, a cash purchaser that takes it as it stands can settle the tax from your proceeds, so you do not have to bring money to the table.

faqs.q: Which office takes Carter County property tax payments?
faqs.a: The sheriff, at 300 West Main Street in Grayson, phone (606) 474-5616. Bills that go unpaid past April 15 are handled by the county clerk.

faqs.q: What if my Carter County tax bill never arrives?
faqs.a: Call the sheriff's office and give your name or parcel number. Ask how it takes payments by mail, and confirm the address before you send a check.

faqs.q: How late can I file a Carter County assessment appeal?
faqs.a: The petition goes to the clerk by the next workday after the May inspection window closes. A conference with the PVA must come first.

faqs.q: Will the Carter County clerk accept my personal check on a delinquent bill?
faqs.a: No. The clerk's page says personal checks are refused on delinquent bills and lists cash, money orders, company checks and cards instead. Card payments carry a user fee.

faqs.q: Can I list my Carter County house while back taxes are open?
faqs.a: Yes. The payoff is taken from your proceeds at closing, so get written balances from the sheriff and the clerk before you sign a contract.
